file.content:
<Enter> allows for creating new lines, like Ctrl/Cmd+Enter sends it to
        the ${HarnessIntegrationScope}

        Sending is never blocked by the harness working: while it is, the send
        button reads "Queue" and sending adds the prompt to prompt mode's
        queue. The button is only disabled while the input is empty.

    tabs:
        The input and send button live inside the body of a tab bar, using
        gpui-kit's default tab styling. The two tabs are Code and Spec.

        Pressing <Tab> while in the chat input cycles between the tabs, and
        focus remains in the chat input.

    systemPrompt:
        The selected tab is the mode a prompt is sent in, and each mode gives
        the hidden anchor a systemPrompt property alongside its userPrompt.
        The code location is `codeRoot` and the spec location is `root`, as
        set in the project's piton.config.pi.

        code:
            We're working on the code located in <code location>. Don't edit
            the spec located in <spec location>.

        spec:
            We're working on the spec located in <spec location>. Don't edit
            the code located in <code location>.

        A prompt keeps the mode it was sent in while it waits in the queue.

content.text:
I made the + half the height of a tab and placed it on top of the line where the Code and Spec tabs meet, so it overlaps both. When + is selected, both tabs now show as selected and the line between them is covered, so they look like one tab. All 14 chat input tests pass, but I haven't run the app to look at it, so it still needs checking by eye.

What changed in `src/chat_input.rs`:

- **Size:** the + is now 16px, half the 32px height of gpui-kit's tabs (it was 26px). The icon scales down with it.
- **Overlap:** Code and Spec now sit right next to each other, with no gap for the +. To find where Code ends, I put an invisible copy of the Code tab bar behind the +. That places the + correctly whatever the width of the Code label, and doesn't make it jump on the first frame. The + has the window's background colour behind it so the tab edge doesn't show through.
- **Unified tab:** selecting + selects both tabs, and a 2px strip in the selected-tab colour hides the two borders where they meet.
- **Test:** I renamed the layout test to `plus_tab_overlaps_the_tabs`. It now checks that the + is square, half the tab height, overlaps both tabs, and is centred on the seam both ways. No test covers the unified highlight, because the test helpers can't read tab colours or selected state.

The + still turns primary (the accent colour) when it's selected. If that's too loud on top of the unified tab, I can keep it as a plain outline instead.
